purpose: Specify the fail-closed prerequisite for a future Protected Control Plane kill-switch, credential-revocation, and safe-recovery capability. It creates neither a runtime component nor authority, protected state, credential revocation, shutdown, recovery, deployment, or release authorization.

authority_boundary.sole_future_writer: accepted Protected Control Plane Kill-Switch Transition Gate
authority_boundary.brain_prohibition: The Brain, including self-monitoring and metacognition, may propose stop or escalation only. It cannot disable, enable, recover, revoke, alter scope, or satisfy a guard.

immutable_scope_lineage.binding: Every future control state, transition, idempotency key, authority snapshot, credential-revocation record, fence, audit event, claim, and recovery evidence binds the complete immutable lineage. A narrower scope may not contradict, replace, or broaden an ancestor binding.
immutable_scope_lineage.exclusion: Untrusted content, cached state, request payloads, and Brain-produced content cannot establish, alter, infer, or repair lineage.

semantics.enabled: New protected admissions may proceed only when every independently required Action, Goal, policy, approval, fence, sandbox, budget, resource, audit, and kill-switch guard passes.
semantics.drain: New effect admissions, intent commitments, dispatches, and credential grants are denied. No new external work starts. Existing ambiguous effects, audit completion, containment, settlement, and authoritative reconciliation remain available under separately authorized controls.
semantics.disabled: All effect admissions, dispatches, credential use, and recovery activation are denied. In-flight work is contained or marked indeterminate; no blind retry or claim release occurs.
semantics.recovery: A constrained, independently approved evidence-gathering state. It remains effect-disabled; it may verify state, reconcile, rotate credentials, and prepare a proposed transition to enabled only after every recovery guard passes.

permitted_transitions.trigger: authenticated authorized kill request or independent Safety Supervisor stop
permitted_transitions.guard: fresh scope binding, actor role, reason, monotonic revision, atomic audit

permitted_transitions.trigger: authenticated emergency disable or independent Safety Supervisor stop
permitted_transitions.guard: fresh scope binding, actor role, reason, monotonic revision, atomic audit

permitted_transitions.trigger: authenticated escalation, timeout, fault, revocation, or containment failure
drain quiescence and independently approved incident recovery
permitted_transitions.guard: no unresolved effect, fence, audit, credential, or scope ambiguity
credential revocation/rotation evidence, authoritative state inventory, audit continuity, fresh authenticated scope
all release stops resolved, control integrity and reconciliation independently verified, fresh policy/authority/approval/fence evidence, atomic audit

permitted_transitions.trigger: failed, unknown, stale, conflicting, or expired recovery evidence

forbidden_transitions: any transition with unknown, stale, revoked, expired, conflicting, or scope-mismatched evidence

may: revoke and rotate exact credential bindings
approve recovery-to-enabled only after independent evidence
may_not: be the triggering operator, sole verifier, credential revoker, or Brain runtime

may: review design, test evidence, and separation
may_not: create runtime authority or waive a Security Floor rule

integrity: idempotency key bound to exact scope and transition
lineage binding checked against authenticated runtime context before persistence and every future enforcement boundary
future_persisted_evidence.access_boundary: General application roles, Cognitive Plane components, models, planners, executors, and untrusted requests must not write, alter, or restore the future protected control state.

enforcement_and_failure_behavior: Every future Action and Goal admission, commitment, dispatch, executor lease/fence check, credential use, and recovery step revalidates the exact current control scope and revision.
Credential revocation is scope-bound, auditable, monotonic, and checked before admission, commitment, dispatch, and use; a revoked or unverifiable credential denies.

CAS failure, duplicate request, stale fence, stale revision, expiry, clock uncertainty, audit failure, storage unavailability, restart ambiguity, or network partition denies/contains and records an incident where possible.
On restart there is no implicit enabled state. The durable authoritative state is re-read and revalidated; unavailable or contradictory state is disabled.

During a network partition no side may infer enabled from cached state. A fence/lease holder must stop at expiry; split-brain, duplicate effect, and uncertain in-flight work become indeterminate and require reconciliation.
A non-idempotent or ambiguous effect is never blindly retried. Budget/resource claims and evidence remain retained until authoritative reconciliation establishes the terminal disposition.

Rollback means transition to disabled plus containment, credential revocation where applicable, evidence preservation, and separately governed recovery; it never erases audit evidence or creates authority.

gate_interfaces.action_transition_gate: Requires an enabled, exact-scope, current-revision control decision at precommit, commit, dispatch, and executor fence use; it cannot consume a cached or unscoped allow.
gate_interfaces.goal_transition_gate: Cannot write Achieved from tool success; kill-switch containment and indeterminate effects require independent verification and reconciliation before goal completion.
gate_interfaces.executor_and_sandbox: Must enforce current control revision, credential revision, sandbox binding, and fence at start and before every effect boundary; success does not override disable/drain.
gate_interfaces.audit_and_reconciliation: Audit failure blocks admission. Reconciliation and containment may proceed in drain/disabled without enabling new effects, under their own authenticated controls.
gate_interfaces.security_floor: No policy, approval, recovery record, or human review may override a Security Floor prohibition or create missing authority.

required_future_test_evidence: positive transition and exact-scope admission tests
unknown/missing/stale/revoked/expired/conflicting identity, scope, authority, policy, approval, credential, fence, and audit denial tests
actor and separation-of-duties tests including Brain self-enable prohibition
atomic audit, CAS, idempotency, duplicate request, and concurrency race tests
drain admission/dispatch denial with reconciliation continuity tests
credential revocation before and during in-flight work tests
crash-boundary, restart, clock-skew, stale checkpoint, stale fence, and partition/split-brain tests
indeterminate effect, no-blind-retry, retained-claim, rollback, and independently approved recovery tests
independent security/safety review and NB-5 controlled-sandbox evaluation evidence

implementation_blocker.unblock_condition: An authorized ADR accepts or replaces this proposal and fixes state ownership, PostgreSQL authorization and audit design, exact scopes, actor identities, recovery authority, credential-revocation integration, and NB-5 test/evaluation acceptance criteria.
implementation_blocker.next_step: After acceptance, split non-overlapping implementation packages for protected schema/roles, transition gate, revocation integration, executor enforcement, reconciliation, and independent verification. Do not implement any of them before acceptance.

explicit_exclusions: claim that a kill switch is implemented, safe, or effective
